_note: Robots.txt product tokens checked by ai-search-readiness. purpose: 'search' = builds an index used to show and cite pages in AI answers; 'user' = fetches a page because a user asked the assistant to; 'training' = collects data for model training (blocking it does not remove you from AI search answers); 'search-engine' = classic web search crawler that AI features also build on. Descriptions summarize each operator's own documentation; check the linked page before relying on details.

crawlers.description: Google Search crawler. Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode use pages from the normal Search index, so blocking it removes you from those too.
Bing Search crawler. Microsoft Copilot answers are grounded in the Bing index.
Crawls pages so they can be surfaced and linked in ChatGPT search results. Not used for training.
Fetches a page when a ChatGPT user (or a GPT action) asks for it. Not used for training.
Collects content that may be used to train OpenAI's foundation models.
Crawls pages to improve the quality of search results in Claude.
Fetches a page when a Claude user asks a question that needs it.
Collects public web content that may be used to train Anthropic's models.
Indexes pages so they can be surfaced and linked in Perplexity answers. Perplexity says it is not used to train foundation models.
Fetches a page in response to a user's question. Perplexity documents that it generally ignores robots.txt because the fetch is user-requested.

A robots.txt control token, not a separate crawler (crawling is done by Google's normal user agents). Controls whether content may be used for Gemini models; Google says it does not affect Google Search ranking or inclusion.
A robots.txt control token (Applebot does the crawling). Opts content out of training Apple's generative AI models; pages can still appear in Siri and Spotlight results.
Builds the open Common Crawl web archive, which is widely used as AI training data.
ByteDance's crawler, widely reported to collect data for training its LLMs.
Crawls the web for use cases such as training Meta's AI models and improving products by indexing content directly.
